newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Debuting Digitel fails to boost Philippine shares.
newsitem.headline: Debuting Digitel fails to boost Philippine shares.

text.p: * Composite index sheds 8.63 points at close
Manila shares remained weak on Wednesday despite the listing of Digitel shares which was expected to boost liquidity in the market, brokers said.
"The market is not moving anywhere. There's no definite macroeconomic news to influence trading," Caesar Tanquingcen, a trader at Connell Securities said.
The much-awaited nine-month GNP figures are not due until later this week.
Digitel debuted poorly, losing 45 centavos from its offer price on its first day to close at 2.55 pesos in heavy trade.
Penny stocks hogged the attention of local investors, since many would like to remain liquid during the Christmas season. "Nobody wants to tie up his funds for too long," he said.
The composite index slipped 8.63 points, or a meagre 0.28 percent, to close at 3,065.65 points after vacillating in a narrow band.
BPI Capital Corp's senior investment analyst Spencer Yap said he expected the market to recover after the announcement of the GNP figures.
